JUN 242024 ANGELINA DINGLASAN Authorized Lotto Agent Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office geedinglasan41@gmail.com 0905-3948945/0927-8941040 Dear Ms. Dinglasan: This has reference to your electronic mail dated March 19, 2024 regarding your request for exemption from business permit pursuant to Republic Act No. 1169 otherwise known as "An Act Providing for Charity Sweepstakes Horse Races and Lotteries". At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight Sections I and 2 of PD No. 7711, a national law, which expressly revoked the authority of local governments and chartered cities to issue license, permit or any form of franchise to operate, maintain and establish other forms of gambling, and provides that all permit or franchise to operate, shall only be issued by the national government. Correspondingly, pursuant to Republic Act No. 1169, the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) was created to be the principal govemment agency for raising and providing for funds for health programs, medical assistance and services, and charities of national character. In line with this, the PCSO shall have the sole and exclusive authority to hold and conduct lotteries. Moreover, in the case of "Lina v. Pano" (G.R. No. 129093, 30 August 2001), the Supreme Court ruled that lotto is regulated by the PCSO. At this juncture, while this Departrnent recognizes that legal opinions are not part of the laws of the land and therefore, cannot be controlling, however, we would like to emphasize that these opinions, such as that of the Department of Justice, have persuasive effect and/or the degree of persuasiveness. 'Section 1. — Any provision of law to the contrary notwithstanding, the authority of Chartered Cities and other local governments to issue license, permit or any form of franchise to operate, maintain and establish horse and dog race tracks, jai-alai or other forms of gambling is hereby revoked. " Section 2 — "Hereafter all permit or franchise to operate, maintain and establish xxx and other forms of gambling shall be issued by the national government upon proper application and verification of the qualifications of the applicant xxx". "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Accordingly, this Department deems it proper to highlight DOJ Legal Opinion No. 71 series of 1995, which clarified that while Sections 447 and 458 of the Local Government Code of 1991 gives provinces and cities/municipalities the authority to regulate businesses within their respective territories and impose license fees, it does not have the power over national government, its agencies and instrumentalities, such as the PCSO. Moreover, such exemption inures to the benefit of its agents such as duly appointed sales agents, as they are mere extensions of the PCSO. It is in this regard that we highlight the purpose of a mayor's I business permit, which is to serve as a "license to operate", and is required for businesses to legally function or operate legally. Its issuance is dependent on whether all or not all the requirements set forth by law or ordinance for its issuance are met/submitted. Hence, to allow cities/ municipalities to require lotto outlets, which are agents of the PCSO, to obtain business permits, would be a circumvention of Sections I and 2 of PD No. 771. It will create an absurd situation wherein mere creatures of the State will be able to defeat national policies under the quise of "regulation"2. Consistently, we reiterate that Sections 1 and 2 of PD No. 771, expressly revoked the authority of local governments and chartered cities to issue license, permit or any form of franchise to operate, maintain and establish other forms of qamblinq, and all permit or franchise to operate, shall only be issued bv the national qovernment. Thus, even as we recognize that the Constitution guarantees local autonomy to LGUs, notwithstanding, settled is the rule that the national legislature is still the principal of local govemment units, which cannot defy its will, modify, or violate it. In view of the foregoing, it is incumbent for us to emphasize that while the local government units enjoy local autonomy and are empowered to issue the necessary orders within their jurisdiction pursuant to the to the general welfare clause provided under Republic Act No. 7160 or known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", however, it must, at all times, make sure that such orders, issuances and acts are in harmony and compliant with existing policies of the national government. In that regard, we are of the considered view that, notwithstanding that you have paid the Mayor's Permit fee, you are entitled to a refund due to an erroneous exaction by the city government. Hence, it is in this regard that we would like to stress that, aside from admonition including reprimand and/or issuance of show cause orders, failure to abide by the directives of the national government, such as repeated violation of rules and regulations could lead to the filing of the appropriate charges against the local chief executive. Be that is it may, please be informed that we have endorsed this matter to our concerned Regional Office, for their appropriate action. 2 Manila International Airport Authority v. Court of Appeals, et al.; G.R. NO. 155650, July 20, 2006 Page 2 of 3

This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. J I T R. LLAMAS Unde r ry for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS LLA/ ULLLS-LRALLD/rjki COPY FURNISHED: ARIEL O.
